record.paper_title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems
record.original_question: Consider the uniform spanning tree on a fine square-grid approximation of a torus. The dual graph formed from the dual edges perpendicular to primal edges not in the tree contains exactly three edge-simple closed paths, each of which is non-null-homotopic. Determine the joint distribution of the three homotopy classes represented by these closed dual paths, as a function of the geometry of the torus.

evidence.quote: There is a random graph dual to the tree, which consists of the dual edges perpendicular to primal edges not in the tree. It is not hard to see that this random dual of the tree contains precisely three edge-simple closed paths (i.e., no repeating edges), and that these paths are not null-homotopic.
Problem 6.2. Determine the distribution of the triple of homotopy classes containing these three closed paths.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}^2/\Lambda$ be a flat torus, where $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a rank-two lattice, and for each small $\delta > 0$ let $G_\delta$ be a fine square-grid graph that approximates $\mathbb{T}$ (the vertex set is a $\delta$-mesh on $\mathbb{T}$, and the edges connect nearest neighbors, with the grid wrapping around in accordance with $\Lambda$). Let $T_\delta$ be a uniformly chosen spanning tree of $G_\delta$. Form the dual graph $D_\delta$ on the faces of $G_\delta$ consisting of exactly those dual edges that are perpendicular to primal edges not belonging to $T_\delta$.

It is a fact that $D_\delta$ contains precisely three edge-simple closed paths $\gamma_1^\delta, \gamma_2^\delta, \gamma_3^\delta$ (paths with no repeated edges), and that each of these paths is non-null-homotopic in $\mathbb{T}$. Each $\gamma_i^\delta$ therefore represents a nonzero element $[\gamma_i^\delta] \in \pi_1(\mathbb{T}) \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$ (up to inversion and choice of basepoint), and we set this triple of free-homotopy classes as $\bigl([\gamma_1^\delta],[\gamma_2^\delta],[\gamma_3^\delta]\bigr)$, viewed as an unordered triple of primitive elements of $H_1(\mathbb{T};\mathbb{Z})/\{\pm 1\}$.

Determine, as $\delta \to 0$, the joint distribution of the (unordered) triple of homotopy classes $\bigl([\gamma_1^\delta],[\gamma_2^\delta],[\gamma_3^\delta]\bigr)$, expressed explicitly as a function of the conformal/geometric shape of the torus $\mathbb{T}$ (i.e., its modular parameter).

Related work on UST scaling limits exists, but no source verifying a complete answer was found, so the status is treated as unknown (most likely still open).
